deliverables.structure: reads mcp-ssot.json; emits v3 rows {kind: front|remote-auth|stdio-lazy, url|cmd, keys[], aliases[], band, note, desc_sha8_baseline}; duplicate-alias lint FAILS non-zero on any dup; drift gate wired into gen_context --check

single asyncio process on 127.0.0.1:31150 (fallback 31151-31159); per-server path router /mcp/<name>; per-request lifecycle: resolve row (unknown => 404 + FAILED audit) -> auth stub -> poison/dead check (poisoned => 503) -> proxy to front; append-only audit JSONL audit/gw-YYYYMMDD.jsonl with immutable S6 vocabulary SUCCESS/FAILED/INTERRUPTED + supersedes corrections + req/resp sha8 + resolved_model attribution; lazy lifecycle: spawn-on-first-initialize, refcount on initialize/disconnect, 30-min idle exit, port-guarded idempotent start (NO scheduled task, NO always-on slot); two meta-tools: gateway.catalog, gateway.dead_list

deliverables.scope: cve + semgrep remotes in cyberstrike.json pointed at http://127.0.0.1:31150/mcp/cve and /mcp/semgrep; generated/direct-fallback.json kept warm for rollback

what_the_skeleton_proves: 1. Collapses the design's headline UNVERIFIED: the TUI remote-MCP client accepts per-server distinct paths on one host:port (tools/list + one tool call succeed with byte-identical tool names mcp__cve__*, mcp__semgrep__*)
2. Added latency < 5 ms p95 for the local hop (vs 300000 ms TUI timeout)
3. Lazy spawn + refcount + idle exit does NOT become an always-on service (G-12 owner constraint honored; process absent when no clients)
4. Audit discipline catches the CS-2 stuck-call signature: black-hole a front => sweep reports the never-terminal call_id; audit lines are never rewritten
5. Dead-list both-states control: stop the semgrep front => mount receipt + gateway.dead_list report dead; restart => mounted (detector must fire in the broken state)
